definitions.content: ABS Transaction Fee: means the fee payable to the lender upon voluntary cancellation or prepayment in connection with an ABS transaction, typically calculated as a percentage of the prepaid amount to compensate for lost interest income or as an exit fee structured to facilitate the refinancing of the assets into a securitization.

Acceptance: means the formal act or notice by the Purchaser confirming its acceptance of an Offer to Sell Receivables delivered by the Seller, which effectuates the sale, transfer, and assignment of the specified Receivables and Related Security from the Seller to the Purchaser under the Receivables Purchase Agreement.

Account Acceleration Notice: means a notice to be delivered to the Issuer Account Bank, typically substantially in the form set out in the Issuer Account Bank Agreement and executed by the Cash Manager, which serves to instruct the bank regarding the control, freezing, or transfer of the Issuer Accounts (usually following an Event of Default or Servicer Termination Event).

Accounting Reference Date: means the specific date in each calendar year on which the Issuer's financial year ends, as designated in the transaction documents, used for determining deadlines for financial reporting and audit requirements.

Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers Concentration Percentage: means the ratio, expressed as a percentage, of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Loans to Prime Borrowers that have been subject to modifications or adjustments to their original terms (such as forbearance, extensions, or interest rate reductions) relative to the Aggregate Principal Balance of the entire Portfolio, as calculated to ensure compliance with the specific concentration limits outlined in the Transaction Documents.

Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount: means the calculated amount by which the aggregate outstanding principal balance of Loans to Prime Borrowers that are subject to Adjusted Loan Terms exceeds the applicable Concentration Limit percentage allocated to such category of Loans, which excess amount is typically excluded from the Borrowing Base or assigned a zero value for collateral valuation purposes.

Adjusted Loan Terms Near Prime Borrowers Concentration Percentage: means the maximum percentage of the Aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of the Portfolio that may consist of Receivables owed by Near Prime Borrowers subject to adjusted loan terms (such as modifications, forbearance, or extensions), as specified in the Concentration Limits.

Adjusted Loan Terms Near Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount: means the portion of the aggregate outstanding principal balance of loans to near-prime borrowers with adjusted terms that exceeds the specific maximum percentage or concentration limit allocated for such loans in the portfolio, often resulting in that excess portion being assigned a zero value for borrowing base calculations.

Affected Person Tax Credit: means a credit, relief, remission, or repayment in respect of any Tax obtained by an Affected Person (such as a Lender or Finance Party) that is attributable to a Tax Payment or an Increased Cost payment made by an Obligor, typically requiring the Affected Person to pay an amount to the Obligor equal to the benefit received to ensure the Affected Person is not over-compensated.

After Tax Basis: means a basis of calculation ensuring that a payment is made in an amount which, after deduction or payment of any taxes required to be paid by the recipient in respect of such payment, leaves the recipient with the net amount it would have received had no such taxes been payable.

APR: means Annual Percentage Rate, representing the total cost of credit to the consumer expressed as an annual percentage of the total amount of credit, calculated in accordance with the mathematical formulas and assumptions prescribed in the FCA Consumer Credit Sourcebook (CONC) and applicable consumer credit legislation.

Assignment Agreement: means the agreement entered into between an existing lender and a new lender for the assignment and transfer of all or part of the existing lender's rights and obligations under the Senior Facility Agreement or the Mezzanine Facility Agreement, substantially in the form prescribed in the schedules to the respective facility agreement.

Back-up Servicer Invocation Notice: means the written notice delivered to the Back-up Servicer (or Standby Servicer) instructing it to assume the active responsibilities and duties of the Servicer under the Transaction Documents, typically triggered by the occurrence of a Servicer Termination Event, insolvency of the incumbent Servicer, or other defined default events.

Back-up Servicer Invocation Plan: means the operational plan and procedures set out in the Back-up Servicing Agreement detailing the steps, data transfer protocols, and timelines for transitioning servicing responsibilities from the Servicer to the Back-up Servicer upon the occurrence of a servicer termination event or default to ensure continuity of collection and administration.

Blocking Action: means the exercise of a voting right or veto by a creditor or class of creditors to reject or prevent a Basic Term Modification (such as changes to maturity dates, interest rates, principal amounts, or payment priorities) under the Master Framework Agreement, typically requiring a higher consent threshold or unanimous approval to pass.

Break Costs: means the amount necessary to compensate a lender or finance party for any loss or expense incurred (including the cost of breaking funding arrangements) as a result of the receipt of a payment of principal or unpaid sum on a day other than the last day of the applicable interest period. This is typically calculated as the difference between the interest which the lender would have received for the remainder of the period and the amount which the lender would be able to obtain by placing an amount equal to the principal received on deposit for the same period.

Cash Management Services: means the services provided by the Cash Manager under the Cash Management Agreement, which typically include the operation of the Issuer's bank accounts, calculation of the application of funds in accordance with the priority of payments, and the preparation of investor reports and maintenance of ledgers.

Cash Manager Termination Event: means specific events upon the occurrence of which the appointment of the Cash Manager may be terminated, typically including insolvency of the Cash Manager, failure to make required payments or calculations, or material breach of obligations under the Cash Management Agreement.

Cash Manager Termination Event Notice: means a written notice delivered by the Issuer to the Cash Manager terminating the Cash Manager's appointment and obligations under the Cash Management Agreement following the occurrence of a Cash Manager Termination Event (such as insolvency, default, or material breach).

Cash Manager Website: means the internet website maintained by the Cash Manager (or its agent) where the Monthly Investor Reports, quarterly reports, and other relevant transaction information and data are made available to the Noteholders, Rating Agencies, and other authorised parties.
